title: DeviceToGateway
description: Messages a phone sends to the gateway.

oneOf.description: Answer to exactly one [`GatewayToDevice::Command`].
The owner changed capabilities or session settings.
The device is closing the session on purpose (stop button, unpair, expiry).
Since 1.4: the phone is waiting for the owner's answer to an approval.
One action, such as a tap on "Send".
Letting the AI use an app at all.

ApprovalRequest.description:
The phone is waiting for the owner to answer an approval for a running
command (since 1.4). Gateways keep waiting for that command's result
while it is open, and may relay an answer when `remote` is true.

choices.description: The answers the phone offers; `deny` is always possible.

command_id.description: The command the approval belongs to.

expires_at_ms.description: Unix ms (device clock) when the phone stops waiting.

nonce.description: Random, 32 lowercase hex characters; an answer must quote it.

remote.description: The owner allows answering from the AI app (their `remote_approvals` switch).

title.description: What the owner is asked, e.g. "Tap “Send” in com.example.chat". Untrusted app text may appear quoted.

Capability.description:
A named, separately grantable device capability.

Capabilities are what the phone owner switches on and off. Every command
maps to the capabilities it needs (see [`crate::Command::required_capabilities`]);
a command whose capabilities are not all enabled is refused before it
reaches the platform.

oneOf.description: Device model, OS version, screen size, and session state.
Read a redacted tree of on-screen UI elements.
Take a screenshot of the current screen.
Tap, long-press, and swipe.
Type text into an editable, non-sensitive field.
Press back, home, or recents.
List launchable apps and open one.
Since 1.6: list and read allowed photos, Latch's downloads, and the picked folder.
Since 1.6: save, rename, and delete files in those places.
Since 1.6: open an app's share screen with files.
Since 1.7: put text on the clipboard (never read it).

CapabilityStatus.description: Whether a capability can be used right now on a specific device.

oneOf.description: The owner switched it on and the OS permission is granted.
The owner has not switched it on (the default for everything but `device.info`).
The owner wants it but an OS permission is missing.
This platform or OS version cannot provide it.

DeviceDescriptor.description: Static facts about the phone, sent once per connection.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable failure codes.

Every failure anywhere in the system maps to exactly one of these. Codes
are part of the public contract: never rename one, only add.

oneOf.description: The request was malformed or violated a protocol limit.
The device does not offer this capability on this platform.
The owner has not enabled a required capability, or an OS permission is missing.
Policy refused the operation outright.
The operation targets a password, OTP, or otherwise sensitive element.
The screen changed since the referenced observation.
The referenced element no longer exists or is not actionable.
The app marked its window as secure; the OS refused capture.
The owner denied the approval request.
The approval request was not answered in time.
The operation was cancelled before it ran.
The device did not answer before the deadline.
No device is connected, the session is paused or stopped, or it ended.
More than one device is online and none was named.
A transient transport problem; retrying may help.
A bug in Latch. Please report it with the correlation id.

Hello.description: First message on every device connection.

device_time_ms.description:
Device clock (Unix ms) when the message was sent, so the gateway can
interpret `session.expires_at_ms` despite clock skew.

ProtocolError.description:
A typed protocol failure with a message that is safe to show and log.

Messages must never contain screen text, tokens, or personal data.

SessionInfo.description: The owner's current session settings on the phone.

approve_every_action.description: When true the owner wants to approve every action, not only risky ones.

expires_at_ms.description: Unix epoch milliseconds after which the phone stops accepting commands.

paused.description: When true the owner paused the session; commands are refused.

remote_approvals.description:
Since 1.4: the owner lets approvals be answered in the AI app as well as
on the phone. The gateway then asks the AI app's user (MCP elicitation)
whenever the phone sends an [`ApprovalRequest`] marked `remote`.
